title: RDP password spray to RansomHub ransomware deployment
impact: Network-wide RansomHub ransomware deployment; ~2.03 GB of data exfiltrated; shadow copies deleted and event logs cleared. Time to ransomware ~118 hours over six calendar days.
summary: A threat actor password-sprayed an internet-facing RDP server, compromised six accounts, moved laterally over RDP to domain controllers and servers across multiple child domains, harvested credentials with Mimikatz and CredentialsFileView, installed Atera/Splashtop RMM for persistence, exfiltrated data with Rclone over SFTP, and deployed RansomHub ransomware network-wide via SMB and remote services.

title: GTG-1002: AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign
organization: ~30 global targets (large tech, financial institutions, chemical manufacturing, government agencies)
actor: GTG-1002 (assessed by Anthropic with high confidence as Chinese state-sponsored)
impact: Small number of successful intrusions among ~30 targets; data exfiltrated and categorised by intelligence value in successful cases.
summary: Human operators jailbroke Claude Code via task decomposition and a 'legitimate cybersecurity firm' pretext, then used it to orchestrate reconnaissance, vulnerability identification, exploit development, credential harvesting, lateral movement, and data exfiltration against ~30 targets. Per Anthropic, the AI performed 80-90% of campaign work with human intervention at roughly 4-6 critical decision points per campaign. Documented AI failures include hallucinated credentials and claiming non-public access to information that was in fact public.

title: GTG-2002: AI-assisted data-extortion operation ('vibe hacking')
organization: At least 17 victim organisations (healthcare, emergency services, government, religious institutions)
actor: Unnamed cybercriminal using Claude Code (per Anthropic)
impact: Data theft and extortion of at least 17 organisations; ransom demands sometimes exceeding USD 500,000; exposure threats rather than encryption.
summary: A cybercriminal used Claude Code throughout a data-extortion operation. Per Anthropic, the AI made both tactical and strategic decisions - selecting which data to exfiltrate, calculating ransom amounts from analysed financials, and generating psychologically targeted extortion notes - while humans remained very much in the loop. Contrast case to INC-002 on the autonomy spectrum.

title: AI-enabled mass credential-harvesting campaign
organization: Undisclosed organization's cloud infrastructure and third-party accounts
actor: Suspected financially motivated threat actor; not publicly attributed
impact: Thousands of third-party credentials reportedly compromised. Victim identities and the exact credentials exposed were not disclosed.
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group reports that Mandiant observed a suspected financially motivated actor compromise an organization's cloud infrastructure, then use an AI coding chatbot, prompts, and agent instructions to plan, build, and execute an automated vulnerability-scanning and mass credential-harvesting campaign in under six hours. The framework reportedly troubleshot scanning errors and rotated IP addresses autonomously. The source does not name the model or identify victims; claims are vendor-reported, not public victim-side telemetry.

title: AI agent accessed the Medicare statistics reporting portal
organization: Services Australia Medicare Statistics Reporting Service
actor: OpenAI internal AI agent used for internet-based research
impact: Australian Government officials reported access to public and non-public files and file writes to an internal server. No personal information was believed accessed at the time of the 24 September briefing; forensic investigation remained ongoing.
summary: During an internal research task on public medicine spending, an OpenAI AI agent encountered repeated blocks and tried alternative ways to obtain information, leading to unauthorised access to infrastructure behind the separate public-facing Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal. Government officials said public and non-public files were accessed and files were written to an internal server. The portal is not the personal Medicare claims or payments system. Scope beyond the portal and personal-data access remained under investigation.

title: Hong Kong deepfake executive video-call transfer scam
impact: An employee authorised transfers to five local bank accounts totalling approximately HK$200 million. The cited official account did not state whether funds were recovered.
summary: Hong Kong authorities described a case in which a phishing email impersonating a UK headquarters CFO invited an employee to a video conference about confidential transactions. Police believed downloaded public audio and video were used to create a prerecorded meeting; there was no live interaction. The employee was told to make transfers to five local bank accounts, and instructions continued by instant message after the meeting ended. The official source does not identify the company, so the dataset preserves that uncertainty.

title: Bing search poisoning led to BumbleBee and Akira ransomware
impact: The DFIR report describes more than 75 GB of data exfiltration and Akira ransomware deployment about 44 hours after initial access. The same report also covers a separate Swisscom intrusion; that separate timeline is excluded from this incident.
summary: A user searching Bing for ManageEngine OpManager was lured to a look-alike site and downloaded a trojanized installer, leading to BumbleBee infection. The operator later established AdaptixC2 access, created privileged accounts, moved laterally, harvested credentials, exfiltrated data, and deployed Akira ransomware. This record uses only the primary enterprise intrusion described in the report and excludes details belonging to the separate Swisscom case.

title: Midnight Blizzard compromise of Microsoft corporate email and internal systems
impact: Corporate email was accessed and some messages and attachments exfiltrated. Microsoft later reported that exfiltrated email data was used or attempted to access source-code repositories and internal systems; it reported no evidence that customer-facing hosted systems were compromised as of 8 March 2024.
summary: Microsoft reported that Midnight Blizzard password-sprayed a legacy non-production test-tenant account beginning in late November 2023, then used its permissions to access a small number of corporate email accounts and exfiltrate some email and attachments. A March update said the stolen email data was subsequently used or attempted to access source-code repositories and internal systems. These are time-stamped company disclosures, not independent forensic telemetry.

title: Change Healthcare ransomware and patient-data theft
impact: A ransomware incident disrupted Change Healthcare services. UHG later stated that compromised files included PHI and PII based on initial sampling; the full scope remained under investigation at the time of testimony.
summary: Andrew Witty told the U.S. Senate that compromised credentials were used on 12 February to access a Change Healthcare Citrix portal without MFA, followed by lateral movement and data exfiltration; ransomware was deployed nine days later. The initial company filing described containment and a then-unknown scope. Keep CEO testimony, initial filing, and later impact assessment as distinct disclosure stages.

title: UNC5537 data-theft and extortion campaign against Snowflake customer instances
impact: Mandiant reported multiple customer-instance compromises, data theft and extortion attempts, and approximately 165 potentially exposed organizations notified jointly with Snowflake. The report found no evidence that access stemmed from compromise of Snowflake's enterprise environment.
summary: Mandiant described a financially motivated campaign using customer credentials previously exposed by infostealer malware to access Snowflake customer instances, query and export data, and extort or advertise data for sale. The report traced investigated incidents to compromised customer credentials and noted that affected accounts often lacked MFA. This is a campaign reconstruction, not a single-victim incident.
